c.tagline: A remote southern Red Sea coast nicknamed the 'Egyptian Maldives,' known for dolphins, whale sharks, and untouched reefs
langs: German and Italian (common due to tourism)

card: Widely accepted at hotels and larger restaurants; cash useful for smaller shops

taxi.fare: Negotiated flat rate, as meters are uncommon
taxi.fareNote: Resorts are spread out along the coast, so most transport is pre-arranged through hotels

emergency.note: Tourist police (180) can assist with English-language support

walk: Marsa Alam's resorts are spread along the coast and largely self-contained; a car or hotel transfer is needed to move between areas

safety.safety: Generally safe and low-key; the region is more remote and less developed than Hurghada or Sharm El Sheikh
safety.crime: Very low crime; the main practical concern is the remoteness of some resorts from medical facilities

solo.f: comfortable in resorts; dress modestly outside

hood_landmark.Port Ghalib: Port Ghalib's marina and waterfront promenade
hood_landmark.Marsa Alam Town Center: Marsa Alam's small central market area
hood_landmark.Abu Dabbab Bay: Abu Dabbab Bay's sea turtle and dugong feeding grounds
hood_landmark.Wadi El Gemal National Park: Wadi El Gemal's mangroves and desert wildlife

avoid.reason: Quad-bike, taxi and dive-trip touts overcharge; agree prices in advance and use licensed dive operators.

hood_desc: A purpose-built marina resort town north of Marsa Alam, with the area's most hotels, restaurants, and yacht facilities.
The small original town center, mainly a practical stop for supplies rather than a tourist destination itself.
A protected bay famous for sea turtle and dugong sightings, ringed by a handful of eco-conscious resorts.
A dedicated diving village with one of the region's best accessible house reefs right off the beach.
A vast coastal and desert national park south of town, protecting mangroves, coral reefs, and rare wildlife.

water.note: Drink bottled water only; the desalinated tap supply is not considered potable.

transit.sys: No formal municipal transit; hotel shuttles and pre-arranged transfers are the norm
transit.hours: Transfers arranged around flight and excursion schedules
transit.pay: Cash or pre-paid through the resort
transit.map: Not centrally published; resorts arrange transport and excursions
transit.note: Marsa Alam's resorts are spread along roughly 100 km of coastline, so advance transport planning matters

transport.air: Marsa Alam International Airport (RMF), serving the resort region directly
transport.train: No passenger rail service to Marsa Alam
transport.bus: Limited long-distance bus service; most visitors fly in
transport.car: Rental cars available at the airport; distances between resorts and sites can be significant

net.m: Moderate 4G coverage near resorts, weaker in remote areas
net.ops: Vodafone Egypt, Orange Egypt, Etisalat Misr
net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in hotels
net.ap: A Vodafone or Orange Egypt tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: 10-15% is customary for dive guides and tour operators
tip.r: 10% is standard, often added automatically at resort restaurants
